lessonRef.focus: theoretical distributions and their expected values
lessonRef.title: Publication, presentation, or reflection: theoretical distributions and their expected values

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Notice how the explanation names the reason for each step.

items.prompt: P(A) = 4/10, P(B|A) = 5/10. Find P(A and B).

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A trial succeeds with probability 3/10 and is repeated 2 times independently. Let X count the successes. Find P(X = 0) as a decimal.
From 5 distinct items, how many ways are there to choose 3 and arrange them in order?
A random variable takes values 15, 18, 9, 8 with probabilities 5/10, 1/10, 3/10, 1/10 respectively. Find its expected value.
Given P(A) = 1/10 and P(B | A) = 8/10, find P(A and B) in lowest terms.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Explain your method so that someone who has not done this unit could follow it.

items.prompt: A trial succeeds with probability 1/10 and is repeated 4 times independently. Let X count the successes. Find P(X = 0) as a decimal.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: From 5 distinct items, how many ways are there to choose 4 and arrange them in order?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
